key_decisions: 13 preserves the distinct accounts of the woman and narrator, begin to rescue and until death, and the questions about the boy’s rule and work. The LORD is supplied as the wonder-worker in 19, with the alternative subject noted. The wife’s reasoning answers Manoah’s fear in her own voice.

14 retains right in my/Samson’s eyes, uncircumcised, Spirit and violent lion simile, parental concealment, and both clothing categories. The LORD is chosen as seeking an occasion with the Samson alternative noted. Seventh day follows the pin despite fourth-day alternatives and the three/seven-day tension. The riddle, answer and heifer retort keep their literary form. Thirty men are explicitly killed for clothing.

15 retains reciprocal revenge claims, 300 foxes with jackals alternative, olive orchards with the crop construction explained, the burning of the wife and father to death, hip and thigh, 3,000 Judahites, both ropes and the flax simile. Jawbone/heap wordplay is preserved with a brief note. The water comes from the hollow at Lehi; spirit, revival and spring naming remain.

16 retains the prostitute encounter, exact gate components, eleven hundred silver units per ruler, repeated bonds and ambushes, and the unfinished Hebrew loom condition without importing its Greek expansion. Full-heart disclosure, shaving agency, affliction, eye gouging and prison labor remain. The roughly 3,000 rooftop spectators are distinct from those inside. One of my two eyes is retained in the prayer, with one act of revenge for both eyes noted. The death wish and comparison of killings remain unembellished.

17 retains dedication to the LORD beside image-making, 1,100 versus 200 shekels, the uncertain carved/cast image construction, ephod and teraphim, and the installed/filled-hand idiom. The Judah-clan/Levite tension stays visible. Father/priest and son relationships are not flattened. Micah’s confidence remains his assertion.

18 retains the unallotted-inheritance claim with Joshua comparison noted, the ambiguous oracle before the LORD, the difficult Laish power/security clause and anyone/Aram alternative. All object lists remain distinct, including the missing cast image in 20. The quiet, secure people are killed and their town burned. Displayed Manasseh follows the pinned suspended nun, with Moses explained; no motive for the scribal feature is asserted. Exile and Shiloh notices remain side by side.

19 follows pinned unfaithfulness and house of the LORD, noting anger and my house alternatives. The woman’s role in bringing him inside follows the read tradition. The host’s offer of both women, the husband’s handing over his concubine, rape and abuse remain explicit. Master, hands on the threshold, no answer and twelve-piece dismemberment are retained without deciding the exact time of death.

20 preserves the difference between the Levite’s report and chapter 19. All troop, provisioning, casualty and survivor numbers remain, including 25,100 versus 25,000. Geba is not silently harmonized with Gibeah. The first two divine replies are distinct from the third’s promised victory tomorrow. Phinehas’s full lineage, ark/pronoun alternative, retrospective battle account, uncertain roads/terrain/rest expression, plural towns and gleaning image are recorded. Destruction of towns and livestock remains explicit.

21 distinguishes the two human oaths, the killing order against Jabesh-gilead’s women and children, the 400 captive young virgins, and the later abduction from Shiloh. All geographic bearings are kept. The LORD’s breach attribution remains in the narrator. The elders’ compressed plea in 22 is translated coherently with uncertainty and the supplied otherwise condition explained. The closing refrain exactly repeats 17:6.
